quote: Yeah. I hear you. I hear you now.
stewart_read: Nearly a minute burned on audio confirmation before any real qualification could start — a rocky, low-legitimacy opening.
coaching_implication: Confirm audio connection faster; don't keep talking into presumed silence for 40+ seconds.

stewart_read: Customer's answer is ambiguous/likely confused, and the rep's own correction ('No. That's a single building home') gets talked over rather than cleanly resolved before moving forward.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should have paused and clarified the home type/ownership status cleanly instead of rushing past it.
coaching_implication: Slow down on the verify section — a confused answer here is a flag, not a checkbox to clear.

quote: I don't have the money, and I don't have the, you know, time.
stewart_read: Classic cost/time objection that the schema flags for a flip (their bill/expense framing), but rep used a generic no-upfront-cost reframe instead of anchoring to his actual pain.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read is not supported — there's no bill captured yet to flip, so the rep's generic reframe is the best available tool at this stage, though still weak.
coaching_implication: Even without a captured bill, rep could reframe 'no time' as 'less time than staying on your current bill' to invert rather than just reassure on cost.

quote: They're easy to hook up. You know? If you buy them, they're easy to hook up.
stewart_read: Customer implies some prior knowledge or exposure to solar installs; rep doesn't probe what he means or where that came from.
coaching_implication: A quick 'have you looked into this before?' could have surfaced competitive context or clarified his actual situation.

quote: I've been on the that was that was in the place that I was in at the time
stewart_read: Customer reveals he doesn't currently live at the address on file — a disqualifying detail the rep never clarifies or confirms.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should have stopped to confirm current residence/ownership status before continuing or closing the call.
coaching_implication: When a customer's address story gets confusing, stop and re-verify ownership/residence before proceeding or exiting — this is a potential hard DQ (not homeowner) left unresolved.

quote: I'm not gonna be able to get it done.
stewart_read: Rep accepts the final no with a throwaway line and no attempt at a small ask, callback offer, or clean disqualification confirmation.
coaching_implication: Even on a clear decline, end with a defined next step (recontact later, confirm DQ reason) rather than an open non-close.
